claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.text:
**Good news! You are eligible for Child Benefit for Alex.**

Even though Alex doesn't live with you, you can still claim Child Benefit because:

✅ **You're contributing to Alex's upkeep** - You're paying £30.00 per week, which is more than the Child Benefit amount (approximately £25.60 per week for one child)

✅ **Alex meets the age requirement** - At 8 years old, Alex is under 16

✅ **You live in the UK** - Meeting the residency requirement

✅ **No competing claims** - No other claimant has priority

✅ **No disqualifying factors** - Alex is not in local authority care, not working 24+ hours/week, hasn't started an apprenticeship, and doesn't receive qualifying benefits in their own right

According to the official guidance, you're considered "responsible for a child" if you're "paying at least the same amount as Child Benefit (or the equivalent in kind) towards looking after them - for example on food, clothes or pocket money."

**Important note:** If you or your partner have an individual income over £60,000, you may need to pay the High Income Child Benefit tax charge. However, this doesn't affect your eligibility to receive the benefit itself.

You can proceed with your Child Benefit application!

reasonings:
According to the UK Child Benefit rules, you can qualify for Child Benefit even when the child does not live with you, provided you contribute at least the same amount as the Child Benefit payment (or the equivalent in kind) towards the child's upkeep. 

For Alex:
1. Alex is 8 years old (under 16) - meets age requirement
2. You live in the UK - meets residency requirement
3. Alex does not live with you, but you contribute £30.00 per week towards their upkeep
4. The current Child Benefit rate for one child is approximately £25.60 per week (2024 rate), so your £30.00 weekly contribution exceeds the required threshold
5. No other claimant has priority
6. Alex is not in local authority care, hospital, or fostered
7. Alex does not work 24+ hours per week, has not started an apprenticeship, and does not receive qualifying benefits

The rules state: 'You could continue to get payments for more than 8 weeks if you contribute to your child's upkeep by the same amount or more than the Child Benefit payment. Upkeep includes clothes, presents, food and pocket money and financial contributions to provide your child with somewhere to live.'

Since you are contributing more than the Child Benefit amount weekly and no other person has priority, you are eligible to claim Child Benefit for Alex.
